issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/async-in-depth is titled "Async in depth" / "Подробно об асинхронности" and is cited for "no thread is dedicated to waiting for the response: the request is carried out by the operating system and the device driver".
issues.problem: The fetch redirected to a different page, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-scenarios, titled "Asynchronous programming scenarios". The cited title "Async in depth" no longer matches the page a reader lands on. The visible excerpt shows only that the UI thread is free and that await yields control to the caller. It does not show that no thread is dedicated to waiting on I/O, or that the OS and driver perform the request. The repair note admits the page was not confirmed.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the URL with the canonical https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-scenarios and retitle it "Asynchronous programming scenarios" / "Сценарии асинхронного программирования". Then either soften the claim to what the pages show (await does not block the thread, control returns to the caller, the continuation runs when the task completes), or drop the "no thread is dedicated to waiting / the OS and driver carry out the request" wording from both locales, in explanation paragraph 2 and in optionExplanations.b. Alternatively cite a source whose excerpt states that claim.
